h: Shabbos Rest Completes the Work of the Week

p: בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ג, א)
In Midrash Rabbah (this parsha, Vayikra Rabbah 3:1):
(קֹהֶלֶת ד, ו) טוֹב מְלֹא כַף נָחַת
these are the six weekdays, etc.
that during the six weekdays one earns
only that it is with toil,
while on Shabbos one earns a single handful,
surely on Shabbos one gains a great deal,
and in the merit of honoring Shabbos
And if it refers to the toil and labor,
that on Shabbos it is only one handful
and on the weekdays two handfuls,
for on Shabbos there is no labor at all,
only in the merit of Shabbos";
וְאִם קָאֵי עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
if it refers to the activity of this world,
that it refers to one who is occupied during the weekdays
for the purpose for which he was created,
"He was created for the toil of Torah";
and as they said (Toras Kohanim, Parshas Bechukosai):
And this toil is called "two handfuls,"
in the manner we find regarding Rebbi
And although words of Torah are a toil of the mouth,
is to bring one to action;
and the fulfillment of the positive mitzvos
הוּא עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת אַהֲבָה וָחֶסֶד
comes through the attribute of love and Chessed,
And one who has no yiras Shamayim,
the Torah in his hands is called
"a price in the hand of a fool,"
which are the instruments of action.
And Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
was a chariot for the attribute of Chessed,
and his trait was alacrity in the positive mitzvos,
קְרָא זְרוּזוּתֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן
"The pasuk is teaching us Avraham's alacrity."
And Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
was a chariot for the attribute of Gevurah,
(this parsha, III 12a, at the end of the amud):
עַל מִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה וּמִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
(אִיּוֹב כה, ב) הַמְשֵׁל דָּא אַבְרָהָם כוּ׳
because he holds on to this side and that side;
בְּמִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה וּבְמִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וְכוּ׳
to positive and negative mitzvos," etc.
That is, the positive mitzvos come from love,
וְקִיּוּם מִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה מִצַּד הַיִּרְאָה
and keeping the prohibitions comes from fear,
as Chazal said in the Yerushalmi
being quick to actually do mitzvos,
as is written (in Rashi's commentary on the Rif,
פֶּרֶק א דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לְדַף כ, ב)
chapter 1 of Avodah Zarah, on daf 20b).
And this is "I toiled with my ten fingers in Torah"
And so too the tefillin shel yad
meaning sluggishness so as not to do evil;
for everywhere good action is called
"for those who go to its right,"
and its opposite "for those who go to its left,"
And this is what it says:
that is, the toil of Torah,
with the two arms, right and left,
And Shabbos is "a handful of calm":
the Pesikta and Tanchuma apply it
(הוּבָא בְּבֵית יוֹסֵף אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן רפח)
who toil in Torah all the weekdays,
That is, to receive words of Torah
(יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד) אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה׳
is obligated only in guarding Shabbos,
which is by sitting and refraining
only "remember" is with the mouth for a moment,
וְהַשְּׁאָר הַכֹּל הוּא בְּשֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה
and all the rest is sitting and refraining.
And this is the single handful,
fear and guarding against the prohibitions.
only in the merit of Shabbos,
'Through return and calm you will be saved.'"
they are redeemed through Torah study,
nevertheless the essence of the redemption
is in the merit of Shabbos.
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג הָאָדָם מִדַּת יִרְאָה
through man's attaining the attribute of fear,
for those who keep Shabbos are called "those who fear My Name,"
and "the awe of Shabbos is upon the unlearned,"
and through this they come to teshuvah,
"Through return and calm you will be saved."

from "the heart of the fool, at his left,"
sluggish so as not to do evil,
בָּזֶה לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם שׁוּם עֵסֶק
with this they will have no occupation at all.
וְזֶהוּ טוֹב כַּף נַחַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא
And this is "better a handful of calm," the World to Come,
and striving of spirit" in this world.
that he prefers his own kav:
"his wish is to do his work."
And indeed in Midrash Koheles Rabbah
what is said here is absent:
his wish is to be called one who toils and eats,
which is the World to Come,
which is a semblance of the World to Come;
with satisfaction and the delight of Shabbos.
"And through return and calm you will be saved."
